description: Virtual Singapore is a detailed, semantically enriched 3D digital model of Singapore, built as a collaboration between the National Research Foundation, the Singapore Land Authority, which provides topographical mapping data, and GovTech, which provides ICT expertise, with 3D software from Dassault Systèmes. The semantics mean the model knows what each object is, such as the kind of building and its roof, walls, doors and windows, so that users can, for example, find all roofs of buildings of a certain height or walls facing a given bearing and estimate their sunlight for solar panels. It is designed as a dynamic model that connects to real-time sensor data, such as air quality, temperature and noise, for simulations of pollution, wind flow, urban heat islands, flooding and the traffic and pollution effects of new developments. Coverage: Singapore; the 2017 article reports Yuhua and Teck Ghee modelled first, with other areas to follow from mid-2017. Access: the article says the platform was to be ready for government agencies by 2018 and then opened to the public progressively. Licence: none stated. Caveats: the official SLA and NRF pages for the programme now return 'page not found', so the only provider source read is a GovTech article of 28 March 2017; current access terms were not confirmed. Simulation uses: national-scale solar, flood, heat and planning studies on a semantic 3D city model. Related records: the OGC CityGML standard and the NSW Spatial Digital Twin.
